quote: I was his the moment he decided I would be. He only let me believe I had a choice.
He said forever like it was a threat. I said yes like it was a rescue.
I asked him to be gentle. He said gentle was for men who were afraid to lose you.
He didn't fall for me. He decided on me—and that is the reason I stayed.
Every locked door in me, he opened without hurry, like a man who already owned the house.
He held my ruin in both hands and called it the most beautiful thing he'd ever built.
I was a blade the whole world was afraid to hold. He picked me up by the edge.
He loved me in the dark so completely I stopped being afraid of it.
Danger, they warned me. They never said it would feel like finally being found.
He didn't want the softest parts of me. He wanted the parts that could match him.
I stopped counting the exits the night I realised I'd stopped looking for them.
You were never a choice, he told me. You were the one thing I refused to survive without.
He ruined me so carefully that I thanked him for it.
I should have run. Instead I learned the shape of his hands in the dark.
You are not a soft thing to be kept, he said. You are the reason men like me never sleep.
He wasn't safe. He was just mine—and somehow that turned out to be the same thing.
I gave him the worst of me first. He looked at it like a man reading his own name.
Other men wanted to be loved. He wanted to be the reason I couldn't leave.
He didn't promise to be good. He promised to be there when the good men ran.
I was built out of everyone who left. He stayed just to prove that he could.
He touched me like a secret he had every intention of keeping.
He learned my silences before he ever learned my name.
I wanted to be wanted. He wanted to be needed. We ruined each other beautifully.
He said he'd burn it all down for me. The terrifying part was that I believed him.
Some loves arrive like weather. He arrived like a verdict.
He kept his voice low, and my whole world went quiet to hear it.
I told him I was too much. He said he'd never once been afraid of drowning.
He didn't rescue me. He handed me the knife and stood behind me.
The devil, they said. They forgot to mention how gently the devil says your name.
He wanted the version of me the world was afraid of. So I gave it to him.
He loved me like a debt he refused to ever call paid.
He was the worst decision I ever made—twice.
I was a locked room. He didn't pick the lock; he waited until I opened it myself.
He held my face like it was the only true thing he'd ever been handed.
They warned me he'd break my heart. They never warned me he'd guard it with his life.
I asked what he'd do if I left. He said nothing at all—and that was the answer that kept me.
Come here, he said, and every safe plan I ever made forgot its own name.
He ruined me for gentle men, and I have never once wanted a refund.
I was the storm they told him to avoid. He came out to meet me without a coat.
He loved me in a language the good world doesn't teach. I learned it anyway.
He didn't want forever. He wanted every version of me that ever existed, all at once.
You don't scare me, I said. Good, he answered. You should. I only love you.
I stopped praying to be saved the night I met the thing they were all praying about.
He was made of every warning I'd ever been given. I was so tired of being warned.
They call it obsession in a man like him, and devotion in a man they approve of.
